definitions.gloss: paper-thin difference; razor-thin margin; very slight gap
definitions.explanation: An extremely small difference between two things. Often used to describe the narrow gap between success and failure, genius and madness, or two closely matched competitors.

examples.japanese: ⟦{勝敗|しょうはい}→勝敗：04905_shouhai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{紙一重|かみひとえ}の{差|さ}だった。
examples.english: The difference between victory and defeat was paper-thin.

examples.japanese: ⟦{天才|てんさい}→天才：09934_tensai⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{狂気|きょうき}→狂気：27800_kyouki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{紙一重|かみひとえ}の{差|さ}だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われる→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: They say the line between genius and madness is paper-thin.

examples.japanese: ⟦{合格|ごうかく}→合格：02816_goukaku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{不合格|ふごうかく}→不合格：05139_fugoukaku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{紙一重|かみひとえ}の{差|さ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、あと⟦{一点|いってん}→一点：08894_itten⟧⟦{足|た}りなかった→足りる：01209_tariru⟧。
examples.english: The gap between passing and failing was razor-thin — I was just one point short.

notes:
Literally 'the difference of a single layer of paper,' this expression vividly captures how thin the margin can be between two outcomes. The underlying word ⟦{紙一重|かみひとえ}→紙一重：20434_kamihitoe⟧ (paper-thin) is the core metaphor and can also be used on its own as a noun.

USAGE:
- Frequently appears in the pattern A⟦と→と：00512_to⟧B⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{紙一重|かみひとえ}の{差|さ} (the difference between A and B is paper-thin)
- Classic pairings: ⟦{成功|せいこう}→成功：02638_seikou⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{失敗|しっぱい}→失敗：01636_shippai⟧ (success and failure), ⟦{天才|てんさい}→天才：09934_tensai⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{狂気|きょうき}→狂気：27800_kyouki⟧ (genius and madness)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {紙一重|かみひとえ}の{差|さ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{勝|か}つ→勝つ：01199_katsu⟧: to win by a hair's breadth
- {紙一重|かみひとえ}の{差|さ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{負|ま}ける→負ける：01134_makeru⟧: to lose by a hair's breadth
- {紙一重|かみひとえ}の{差|さ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{助|たす}かる→助かる：01956_tasukaru⟧: to narrowly escape

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{僅差|きんさ}→僅差：11526_kinsa⟧: narrow margin — a neutral, factual term without the vivid imagery
- {際|きわ}どい: close; narrow — describes the closeness of a margin in a more colloquial way
